body.input: Which defence and drone companies expanded to Denmark in 2026?

response.content:
## Defence and Drone Companies That Expanded to Denmark in 2026

Denmark's defence sector saw significant expansion activity in 2026, driven by rising European defence spending and the country's growing drone ecosystem. Here are the key companies and initiatives:

### Major International Expansions

- **Airbus** opened a new office in Copenhagen, establishing a permanent presence in Denmark as the country ramps up defence spending and seeks closer cooperation with European defence suppliers. The move is seen as an opportunity to strengthen partnerships between international prime contractors and local Danish suppliers.

- **Saab (Sweden)** deepened its footprint in Denmark with a SEK 350 million (≈$35M) order from the Danish Defence Acquisition and Logistics Organisation (DALO) for advanced live training equipment, including drone and non-line-of-sight training capabilities for the CV90. Deliveries run 2026–2028, building on a 2025 Combat Training Centre contract that established four training sites.

### Ukrainian Defence Companies

- **Ukrainian drone and defence companies** were formally welcomed to produce in Denmark. During President Zelenskyy's visit to Copenhagen in November 2026, Denmark announced it would buy drones and anti-drone systems from Ukrainian manufacturers for its national drone shield. About 70 Danish company representatives discussed new production projects with the Ukrainian side.

- **Fire Point**, the Ukrainian defence manufacturer developing the FP-7.x interceptor missile for the **FREYJA** pan-European anti-ballistic missile defence system, announced plans to open a FREYJA coordination office in Copenhagen. The programme, launched in July 2026 with nine European partner countries, now has 11 members.

### Danish Drone Ecosystem Growth

- The **Danish Defence drone centre** at HCA Airport in Odense became operational in 2026, employing approximately 100 personnel. The business park adjacent to the airport expanded to support drone and counter-drone enterprises, including companies such as **Quadsat** and **Thunderstrike**.

- **Defence Tech Denmark**, a national accelerator programme, began bringing its first cohort of startups and SMEs into the defence industry in January 2026. Participating companies include drone makers such as **OODALOOP Technologies**, **Hecto Drone**, **Nordic Wing**, **Sky-Watch**, and counter-drone firm **MyDefence**, among others.

### Other Notable Activity

- **Renegade UxS** (Denmark) won a contract for NATO Class 1 mini/micro multirotor strike UAS for the Danish Defence (awarded October 2026).
- **Upteko** won a contract for FPV training UAS for the Danish Defence (awarded July 2026).
- **Estonian defence companies** (including **Milrem Robotics** and **Threod Systems**) conducted a high-level trade visit to Denmark to explore expansion opportunities.
- **Latvian defence industry companies** participated in DALO Industry Days 2026 in Denmark to establish partnerships.
- **Terma's** UK subsidiary **OSL Technology** was selected for NATO's new Counter-Drone Marketplace (launched November 2026), with its Face platform running command and control for Denmark's nationwide counter-drone system.

Denmark's defence ministry announced in late March that it would allocate 725 million kroner ($110 million) for the new military drone testing centre, drawing on lessons learned from the war in Ukraine.

By 2026, around 100 Danish military personnel will be training there as drone operators. The centre will also collaborate with companies and researchers to keep Denmark on the cutting edge of drone technology. [...] "Almost 70 percent of the losses in Ukraine are due to drones," researcher Graae said.

"In the Danish defence industry... we're seeing growth especially in software companies, but also robotics and drone companies," he said.

Jouffroy said the military drone hub would contribute to advances in European technology.

When it comes to components, high-end technology comes primarily from the United States while the lower-end is mainly sourced from China, he said. [...] As drones transform the face of war from Ukraine to Gaza, Denmark is opening a military drone testing centre to develop cutting-edge technology and boost its national defence.

It will be based at Hans Christian Andersen airport in Odense, already home to one of Europe's biggest airspaces dedicated to drone testing.

It has almost 2,000 square kilometres (775 square miles) at its disposal over land and sea at the UAS Denmark Test Centre.
